name: compare

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows both photos and the divider with its handle clearly at once.

tagline: A vertical divider drags across two photos to reveal before and after.
summary: Two images are layered, with the top one clipped to a moving handle. Moving the pointer, or dragging the divider, shifts the seam so the second picture shows through.
appearance: A rounded square frame holds one photo on the left and a pale, blurred second image on the right. A thin vertical line with a small white grip splits them, tinted indigo near the seam.
behaviour: On hover the divider follows the pointer across the frame, showing more of one picture or the other. Leaving resets the seam to the middle; in drag mode it stays where released.
demo_content: A red-rock landscape on one side and a blurred image of hands on the other.
use_when: A retouch, renovation or product change needs a direct before-and-after comparison.
avoid_when: Hover mode snaps back to the middle on leave, so it cannot hold a position without switching to drag mode.
customise: Images, alt text, slideMode, initial percentage, autoplay timing and custom first/second/handle content are props; divider colours are baked into classes.
weight_why: A clip-path update per pointer move, plus a small decorative star field near the line.

a11y.note: The slider is pointer-only with no focusable control, though both images do carry alt text.

issues: The handle grip is small and low contrast against the bright image.
polish_why: Crisp clip and clear divider line; the small handle grip is fiddly to grab.
